craft_notes: Sthāyin: śānta of landing — rest, fulfillment, no-other-standing; autonomy dawning mid-proof. SECOND LANDING: No other can stand — continuity (anusaṃdhāna) gathers both measures; spine in line 2 per L3 note. Rejected: (a) explaining linking → killed: never gloss load terms in song. (b) can→shall → killed: modal shift smuggles necessity. Read aloud: FOR-both, THIS-one END-ground … SO-no-OTH-er CAN-stand.

lines: For both, this one end-ground of all thing-awarenesses —
one through linking alone. So no other can stand.
l4.sanskrit_cite: ubhayo 'py eṣa paryantabhūmiḥ sarvārthasaṃvidām eka evānusandhānād ato 'nyo nopapadyate
notes: line 1 nominal, mirroring verbless SA; spine carried by line 2

reads_against.argmap: What holds both measures? → Continuity alone gathers both measures into one end-ground; no second stands.
c1_essence: What never stood cannot stand another: consciousness fits itself to this and I, orders inert selves by double certainty, and completes severed grasping in self-rest (vv10-15).
The same self twofold — breath-bound atom, unbroken whole — gathers in one continuous end-ground where nothing shows more inert than shining (vv16-18).
